texts: Leaving the zone of apposition open is associated with early reoperation for left AV valve insufficiency, which is what option D means: D.
The zone of apposition (the "cleft") lies between the left parts of the superior and inferior bridging leaflets; closing it, at least partly, gives the left valve a better seal.
Operative mortality is now about 2 to 3 percent, complete heart block occurs in about 1 to 2 percent, and pulmonary hypertensive crises are more common when repair is late.
Patients with Down syndrome do not have more late regurgitation.
In the picture, the door whose cleft was left open keeps leaking and goes back to the workbench, while the stitched one stays dry.
Memory hook: leave the cleft open, and the door comes back.
